label: original-phase positions 5-6 (late in input), gated by previous token
explanation: Fires almost only while the original tokens are being read, at absolute positions t=5 and t=6 (91% of activation mass; t=4 and t=7 hold most of the rest, t<=3 never). It never fires in the copy phase and almost never on <DEL>, so it needs L>=6. Position alone is imprecise: only about half of the t=5/6 steps are active. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends on the previous input token. When prev_tok is e, 0 or b at t=5/6 it fires 98.6% of the time and these give the largest activations (the top examples are mostly the step right after e or 0). f, d, z, w and m give weaker boosts. Other previous tokens often give no activation. The current token has only a weak effect, and first occurrences (in_first) fire more often than repeats. Graded token dependence keeps this from being one clean predicate.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: e, 0, b, f, d, z; least: k, 1, 2, p) and the input two steps back (most: e, 0, b, z, m, g; least: v, s, p, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, t=7.
